one_line_intent: Device-specific reset: perform a normal Function Level Reset, then sleep 250 ms before letting the driver touch certain NVMe SSDs.

architecture_rationale.claim: Some NVMe controllers time out waiting for ready status if the driver touches them too soon after FLR; the delay is a device-specific reset method rather than a change to generic FLR timing so that only affected devices pay the cost.

evidence.excerpt: will timeout waiting for ready status to change after NVMe enable if the driver starts interacting with the device too soon after FLR
resolve this with a device-specific reset quirk to add an additional, heuristically determined, delay after the FLR completes

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: The value 250 ms is an empirical choice, not from a spec or datasheet.

evidence.excerpt: A 250ms delay after FLR has heuristically proven to produce reliably working results for device assignment cases.

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: Return value 0 regardless of pcie_reset_flr() result in reset mode: the FLR outcome is ignored, only the probe path reports capability.

hardware_timing_dependencies.claim: Timing dependency: device needs ~250 ms after FLR before NVMe CC.EN handshakes work; the PCIe spec allows 100 ms, so these parts are out-of-spec in practice.

evidence.excerpt: waits 100ms (the maximum time allowed for FLR completion by PCIe r5.0, sec 6.6.2)

suspected_workarounds.claim: Workaround for device assignment (VFIO/KVM) scenarios: symptoms were VM hangs on guest reboot, not bare-metal failures.

evidence.excerpt: Prevent KVM hang when a Solidgm P44 Pro NVMe is passed through to a guest via IOMMU and the guest is subsequently rebooted.

external_interfaces.claim: Not a fixup hook: dispatched through the pci_dev_reset_methods[] table by vendor/device ID (Intel 0x0953, 0x0a54, Solidigm 0xf1ac); reached via pci_dev_specific_reset() from the PCI core reset path used by VFIO and sysfs reset.

compatibility_certification_sensitive.claim: The device-ID table entries are the compatibility surface: a rebranded or re-IDed drive silently loses the delay.

evidence.excerpt: Intel spun off their NAND and SSD business as Solidigm and sold it to SK Hynix in late 2021.

reasoning.claim: Affects reliability of VM device assignment of specific NVMe SSDs (guest hangs). No data-corruption evidence, but in a virtualised mission system a hung guest after reboot is an availability failure.

historical_lessons.claim: The same failure reappeared in a different vendor's product 5 years later and was solved by adding an ID to the table - evidence that the fix encodes a controller-family behaviour, not a single bug.

evidence.excerpt: A similar issue was identified and patched by 51ba09452d11 ("PCI: Delay after FLR of Intel DC P3700 NVMe") and the same fix can be applied for this case.

change_risks.then: VFIO guest reboot hangs on P3700 / P44 Pro class drives

evidence.excerpt: heuristically proven to produce reliably working results

open_questions: Is 250 ms a lower bound or just the first value that worked? The history does not say.

showcase.title: msleep(250): a 'magic number' that is actually a measured contract with three SSD models
showcase.hook: Looks like an arbitrary sleep. History: added for Intel DC P3700 in VM device assignment (Red Hat bugzilla), 'heuristically determined'; reused in 2023 for a Solidigm drive because Intel's SSD unit became Solidigm - the device table follows the company, not the silicon.
